# Summary {.unnumbered}

We value the carbon sequestration of the 27 Member States of the European Union in 2000, 2006, 2012, 2018 and 2024 at the
country-level social cost of carbon of @ricke2018, which is the damage that one more tonne of CO2 causes in each country alone. The
physical flows are those of the carbon sequestration accounts, which value them at a global social cost of carbon. At the
country-level price, the actual flow of the European Union in {{< fact last_year >}} is worth {{< fact cscc_value_median_2024 >}}
million euro at constant 2010 prices, with a range from {{< fact cscc_value_low_2024 >}} to {{< fact cscc_value_high_2024 >}}
million euro, against {{< fact cscc_global_bn_2024 >}} billion euro at the global price. The central value is close to zero because
{{< fact cscc_negative >}} of the {{< fact cscc_countries >}} countries with a value have a negative country-level social cost of
carbon, and the values of the others offset theirs.

# Introduction

Carbon sequestration contributes to global climate regulation, and most of the damage that it avoids falls outside the country where
it happens. The carbon sequestration accounts therefore value it at a global social cost of carbon. The valuation in this report
asks a narrower question, namely how much of that benefit accrues to the country itself, and it uses for this a price for each
country.

The two valuations answer different questions and should not be added up or used in place of each other. The terms in @tbl-terms
recur throughout the report.

| Term | Meaning in this report |
|:---|:-----|
| Social cost of carbon | The present value of the damage that one more tonne of CO2 emitted today causes over time. |
| Global social cost of carbon | The social cost of carbon summed over all countries of the world. |
| Country-level social cost of carbon (CSCC) | The part of the social cost of carbon that falls on one country. |
| Actual flow | The net CO2 that ecosystems deliver to society after the emissions of land are offset, as in the carbon sequestration accounts. |
| Missed flow | The part of the removals that compensates the emissions of land, as in the carbon sequestration accounts. |
| Low, central and high values | Values at the 16.7 percent quantile, the median and the 83.3 percent quantile of the CSCC. |

: Key terms of the report. {#tbl-terms}

# Results

## The European Union

@tbl-eu sets the value of the actual flow at the country-level price beside its value at the global price of the carbon
sequestration accounts. The central value goes from {{< fact cscc_value_median_2000 >}} million euro in 2000 to
{{< fact cscc_value_median_2024 >}} million euro in 2024. Its sign depends on how the flow is shared between countries with a
negative and a positive price, so it can change between years while the flow changes little. The range between the low and the high
value is wide in every year and includes zero.

::: {#tbl-eu}
{{< datatable cscc_eu_series >}}

Actual flow of the EU27 and its value at the country-level social cost of carbon and at the global social cost of carbon of the
carbon sequestration accounts, in million euro at constant 2010 prices.
:::

## Countries

@tbl-countries shows the value of each country in {{< fact last_year >}}. In {{< fact cscc_negative_value_countries >}} countries the
actual flow has a negative central value, which adds up to {{< fact cscc_negative_value_meur >}} million euro, and the countries with
a positive value add up to {{< fact cscc_positive_value_meur >}} million euro. A country with no actual flow in a year has no value in
that year.

::: {#tbl-countries}
{{< datatable cscc_value_by_country >}}

Actual flow in {{< fact last_year >}}, in thousand tonnes of CO2, and its value at the country-level social cost of carbon and at the
global social cost of carbon of the carbon sequestration accounts, in million euro at constant 2010 prices.
:::

# Limitations

**Price.** The country-level social cost of carbon rests on one family of empirical damage functions, which relate growth to
temperature, and on one scenario and one discount rate. Other damage functions in the same database give different values for each
country, and the sign of the value of several European countries changes between them [@ricke2018]. The values describe emissions
of 2020 and serve every year of the series, as the global price of the carbon sequestration accounts does.

**Negative values.** A negative value means that the damage function expects one more tonne of CO2 to raise the output of the country
in the coming decades. It does not include trade, migration and other links through which the damage abroad reaches the country, and
it does not mean that sequestration harms the country.

**Coverage.** Malta has no value in the database, and its flow is not valued. The values of the European Union add up the other 26
countries.

**Flows.** The physical flows inherit the limitations of the carbon sequestration accounts, which are described in their report.
